items.title: Madesi Sleeps in Beggar's Row
items.location: Riften, Beggar's Row (at night)
items.description: The Argonian jeweler Madesi sells expensive jewelry at the market by day, but after midnight he sleeps in Beggar's Row. Svana Far-Shield even urges him to rent a bed at the bunkhouse.

items.title: Guards Comment on Your Gear
items.location: Guards in any city
items.description: Guards comment on what you wear and wield: they mock an iron sword, praise leather armor for being light and steel or iron armor for being sturdy. In Stormcloak or Legion armor, the reaction depends on whom the guards serve.
tips: Iron sword, steel, leather, hide, ebony and dragon armor, and Thieves Guild armor each get their own line
Imperial guards grumble at Stormcloak armor, and Stormcloak guards at Imperial armor
Elven, glass and fur armor and masks get no comments
In Penitus Oculatus armor: "Can't say I envy you that job"; after "Hail Sithis!": "Not very good at your job, are you?"

items.title: Hit the One in the Middle
items.location: Drunks and bandits in a fight
items.description: Drunks and bandits sometimes shout "Remember... hit the one in the middle!" in combat. It's Paulie's advice from Rocky IV, when Rocky was seeing double.

items.title: Ahlam's Key
items.location: Ahlam, Temple of Kynareth and The Drunken Huntsman, Whiterun
items.description: Nazeem's wife Ahlam carries a key to Wintersand Manor, which doesn't exist in the game. The couple was originally meant to live in their own manor, but they ended up living in The Drunken Huntsman and never visit their farm.
tips: You can pickpocket the key, but it opens nothing
Nazeem and Acolyte Jenssen in the Temple of Kynareth carry the same key

items.title: Levitation in Neloth's Tower
items.location: Tel Mithryn, Solstheim
items.description: Neloth's tower has no stairs: a levitation shaft carries you between the entrance and the living quarters. It's a nod to Telvanni architecture in Morrowind, where levitation was everyday magic.
tips: Leave your follower outside: they may not use the shaft and fall to their death
If you commit a crime and Neloth turns hostile, the shaft stops working

items.title: Voices of the Soul Cairn
items.location: Soul Cairn (Dawnguard)
items.description: Some trapped souls repeat the last words of Vigo the Carpathian from Ghostbusters II, others quote Novembers Doom lyrics. One soul is still hurrying to Alessia's camp, and a farmer soul tends a field of soul husks next to two cows.
tips: Cow souls are a rarity here, and the game never explains them

items.title: The Dragon of Blackreach
items.location: Blackreach, the Silent City: the artificial sun above the central Dwemer fortress (closest to the Great Lift at Mzinchaleft)
items.description: Use Unrelenting Force or shoot an arrow at the huge glowing orb, and the ancient dragon Vulthuryol flies out of the darkness. He doesn't know Alduin has returned, and he fights without taking off again.
tips: You can summon him only once
Bend Will doesn't work on him

items.title: Aegisbane
items.location: Raldbthar near Windhelm, carried by Alain Dufont (the target of "Mourning Never Comes")
items.description: An enchanted iron warhammer, the lost heirloom of Clan Shatter-Shield. If you equip it, Windhelm guards recognize the hammer and recall that Alain and Muiri stole it.
tips: You can't officially return it to the family, only reverse-pickpocket it onto a Shatter-Shield
You can kill Alain without joining the Dark Brotherhood

items.title: Uncommon Taste and the Gourmet
items.location: The cookbook turns up in inns and kitchens; the Gourmet is at Nightgate Inn
items.description: The mysterious Gourmet, author of the cookbook Uncommon Taste, is really the Orc Balagog gro-Nolob. A rare signed copy exists in which he dedicates the book to his old friend Anton Virane, a cook in Markarth.
tips: The Gourmet's secret is revealed in the Dark Brotherhood quest "Recipe for Disaster"
In regular copies the soufflé recipe calls for a "cup" of nutmeg, a lethal dose, while the signed copy from Festus Krex says a "pinch" (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Secrets of the Pawned Prawn
items.location: Riften, Bersi Honey-Hand's shop
items.description: The shop is named after Bersi's fishing boat, which he had to sell. On the dresser by the west wall stands a Dwarven urn, your leverage on Bersi in the Thieves Guild quest "Taking Care of Business".
tips: To the right of the entrance is a Thieves Guild shadowmark
If Bersi dies, his wife Drifa takes over the shop
The basement safe holds "To A Concerned Citizen" letters from the Society of Mercantile Freedom, and Bersi and Drifa argue over 300 septims spent on "spices"

items.title: The Secret of Broken Tower Redoubt
items.location: Broken Tower Redoubt, the Reach, southeast of Karthwasten
items.description: Every Forsworn in the fort except the Forsworn Briarheart is a woman, and the ritual chamber holds a defiled shrine to Dibella. The place is tied to the quest "The Heart of Dibella": Fjotra is held here.
tips: You can climb the rocks to the top of the fort
In a dead end on the second floor, a Dibella statue sits between barrels

items.title: Broken Fang Cave
items.location: Whiterun Hold, west of Whiterun and southeast of Rorikstead
items.description: From the outside it's an ordinary vampire cave, but inside it's a Nordic burial chamber with draugr sarcophagi. It has a soul pentagram, an alchemy lab and a rare human heart.
tips: A handy place to get vampire dust early or to catch vampirism
Coincidence: in the film Dracula Untold (2014) the vampire also lives in a cave on Broken Tooth Mountain. The film came out after the game

items.title: Two Archmage's Robes
items.location: College of Winterhold, Arch-Mage's Quarters; the Hall of Valor in Sovngarde
items.description: The game has a version of the Archmage's Robes without a hood and without the magicka bonus. It lies on a table in the Arch-Mage's Quarters (you can't take it without a patch) and is worn by heroes in the Hall of Valor. With the regular robes you can wear a circlet or a dragon priest mask.
tips: Tolfdir gives you the robes after "The Eye of Magnus"
Sometimes you get two or three sets after the quest

items.title: The Dragonborn's Iron Helmet
items.location: Iron Helmet: sold by blacksmiths, found as loot
items.description: The horned iron helmet is the symbol of Skyrim from the cover and trailers, but in the game its visor sits lower than on the poster. On a female character the horns curl more tightly than on a male one. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Eight or Nine
items.location: Temple of the Divines, Solitude
items.description: The priests greet you in the name of the Eight Divines, and the alcove where Talos's shrine stood is empty: the Empire banned his worship under the White-Gold Concordat. If you take Solitude for the Stormcloaks, the Talos shrine eventually returns and the priests start speaking of the Nine Divines.
tips: Wait a few days after "Battle for Solitude"

items.title: Nine Skulls
items.location: Graywinter Watch, east of Whiterun: at the top of the ramp, right of the entrance
items.description: In this troll cave, nine human skulls are laid out in a neat row, likely a nod to the Nine Divines. Nearby is a camp with two dead bandits and Froki's Bow.

items.title: Thaumaturgist's Hut
items.location: Morthal, Hjaalmarch
items.description: Lami's alchemy shop is named after thaumaturgy, a school of magic from Daggerfall and Battlespire that no longer exists in Skyrim. Upstairs Lami keeps skooma for sale; the video's author also found books about Sheogorath there and suspects she secretly worships him (from the video, unverified).
tips: Lami gives a quest to find a book and raises your Alchemy as a reward

items.title: Skulls with Flowers
items.location: Autumnshade Clearing, north of Goldenglow Estate, the Rift
items.description: The clearing has a spriggan with a bear, and a shallow cave on its west end holds two dead hunters; one has the skill book Father of the Niben (Archery). Near the remains lie skulls with flowers stuck in their eye sockets and noses. (from the video, unverified)
tips: Turn grass down in the settings, or you won't spot the skulls

items.title: The White Stag
items.location: "Ill Met By Moonlight", Falkreath and Bloated Man's Grotto
items.description: The white stag Sinding asks you to track is, in the video author's opinion, a nod to the white stag of the King Arthur legends: in Steinbeck's The Acts of King Arthur a pack of hounds chases a white stag. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Maven's Black Sacrament
items.location: Riften, Black-Briar Manor: basement, room with a master lock
items.description: Behind a locked door in the manor basement are the remains of a Black Sacrament: a skeleton, a heart, human flesh, nightshade, a dagger and the book A Kiss, Sweet Mother. Next to them is Maven's letter to Astrid complaining that the contract still hasn't been fulfilled. The video's author thinks she sent the assassins after you, but the game doesn't confirm it.
tips: Maven's key opens the door; you can pickpocket it from her

items.title: The Real Slaughterfish
items.location: Any body of water in Skyrim
items.description: According to the author, the slaughterfish was modeled on the alligator gar, a real freshwater fish with long jaws and armor of thick diamond-shaped scales that grows up to 3 m (10 ft). (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Society of Mercantile Freedom
items.location: Riften, the Pawned Prawn: the basement safe and Bersi and Drifa's bedroom
items.description: The basement safe holds several copies of the letter "To A Concerned Citizen": a secret merchants' society calls for a fight against the Black-Briars and the Thieves Guild, and a white mark on your shop sign means you agree. The letter isn't used in any quest and looks like a cut quest for Bersi.
tips: You can overhear a quarrel: Bersi found 300 septims for "spices" in the books, and Drifa makes muddled excuses
According to the video, a bottle of skooma lies under the couple's bed

items.title: Dragon Spine Totem
items.location: Soul Cairn: northwest of the teleport well by the building east-southeast of the portal stairs (Dawnguard)
items.description: A dragon's spine sticks out of the ground with a human skull mounted on top, and in front of this grim totem is a pedestal with a black soul gem. Approach it and three bonemen rise from the ground.
tips: You can take the black soul gem from the pedestal
A little to the south lies another dragon skeleton with a human skeleton in its ribcage; inside are ancient Nord gauntlets and a steel sword of shocks

items.title: The Greatest Thief in the World
items.location: College of Winterhold, the Arcanaeum: Urag gro-Shub
items.description: Ask Urag about an Elder Scroll and he says it would be guarded so well that "the greatest thief in the world" couldn't touch it. It's a joke for Oblivion players: there the Gray Fox steals an Elder Scroll.

items.title: Birds on Elven Weapons
items.location: Any Elven weapon
items.description: Birds, wings and feathers are carved into the hilts and blades of Elven weapons (swords, bow, dagger, axes, mace), so they go great with the Nightingale set. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: If You Catch My Drift
items.location: Riften, The Bee and Barb: Romlyn Dreth
items.description: Romlyn secretly sells Black-Briar mead at half price. In the Russian version he says "Savvy?" after a sale, the only character with this line, and it sounds like a Jack Sparrow reference. The English line is "if you catch my drift".

items.title: The Black Arts On Trial
items.location: Windhelm, the White Phial: under the counter; also Falkreath Jail
items.description: A book by Arch-Magister Hannibal Traven on why necromancy was banned. According to the author, the title plays on the book Darwin on Trial.

items.title: The Dragon Under the Mountain
items.location: The Reach, near Karthwasten: a dragon lair under an overhanging cliff (probably Dragontooth Crater)
items.description: The dragon lives right under the mountain, with a nearly abandoned settlement nearby. The author sees a nod to Smaug from The Hobbit: a dragon under the Lonely Mountain with the ruined town of Dale nearby. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Sky Above, Voice Within
items.location: High Hrothgar
items.description: The flags of High Hrothgar bear the dragon words "Lok" (sky) and "Thu'um" (voice). In full it's the motto of the Way of the Voice, and Arngeir says it when he starts and ends a conversation. The name Hrothgar echoes the Danish king Hrothgar from Beowulf.

items.title: Who Stole the Sweetroll
items.location: Raven Rock, Glover Mallory's House: locked basement room (Dragonborn)
items.description: Glover, the only Thieves Guild member on Solstheim, keeps everything tied to his past in a secret room, along with a whole row of sweetrolls. Looks like we found who's been stealing them.
tips: Glover gives you the key after you bring back his Bonemold Formula

items.title: The Bannered Mare and the Prancing Pony
items.location: Whiterun, The Bannered Mare
items.description: The inn's name recalls the Prancing Pony from The Lord of the Rings, and there are horse figures on its roof that few people notice. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Chaurus Rider
items.location: Concept art by Adam Adamowicz; Forgotten Vale (Dawnguard)
items.description: In early concept art the Falmer rode chaurus and carried spears, but this didn't make it into the game. The author sees an echo of the idea in the huge creature remains on Falmer tents in the Forgotten Vale.

items.title: Another Steam Centurion
items.location: Nchardak, Solstheim: the quest "The Path of Knowledge" (Dragonborn)
items.description: When a Dwarven centurion wakes up, Neloth shouts: "Look out, another steam centurion!". That's what centurions were called in Morrowind.

items.title: Nelacar from Morrowind
items.location: Winterhold, The Frozen Hearth
items.description: In Morrowind, the Altmer mage Nelacar lives in the Dunirai Caverns. The names match, but the game never says whether they're the same character.

items.title: Riverwood Came First
items.location: Riverwood
items.description: Riverwood was built before all other settlements and served as the template for Skyrim's other towns. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: No Sun on Solstheim
items.location: Solstheim (Dragonborn)
items.description: You can see stars over Solstheim, but no sun, even in daytime or at sunset. Maybe the ash from Red Mountain hides it. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Revus Sarvani the Author
items.location: Solstheim: the silt strider owner (Dragonborn)
items.description: The silt strider owner shares his name with the author of the skill book Light Armor Forging, which was in Skyrim before the add-on.

items.title: Romeo and Juliet by the Shrine to Peryite
items.location: The Reach, at the foot of the cliff with the Shrine to Peryite, in a nook to the southeast
items.description: Two dead lovers with poisons and a dagger between them: a reference to Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet. Nearby lies a dead Bosmer, and the chest beside him holds the skill book Incident at Necrom (+1 Illusion).

items.title: Orcs vs. Dragon
items.location: Soul Cairn (Dawnguard), northeastern part, by the stairs to the pedestal with Spell Tome: Conjure Mistman
items.description: Dragon remains with an enchanted Orcish battleaxe stuck in the skull and Orcish arrows in the body. According to the video, three Orc souls wander nearby and apparently killed the dragon (from the video, unverified).
tips: The battleaxe is always enchanted, but the enchantment can vary

items.title: Why the Retching Netch?
items.location: Raven Rock, The Retching Netch: Geldis Sadri
items.description: Ask Geldis Sadri about the name. He'll tell you how a naked drunk Dunmer threw a bottle of sujamma at a netch and it threw up. It's a reference to a similar scene in the film Twister (1996).

items.title: 'Tis But a Scratch
items.location: Bandits all over Skyrim, in combat
items.description: A wounded bandit sometimes shouts "'Tis but a scratch!". The video's author thinks it's a reference to the Black Knight in Monty Python and the Holy Grail (1975) (from the video, unverified).

items.title: Whiterun and Rohan
items.location: Whiterun, Dragonsreach
items.description: The video's author compares Whiterun to Rohan from The Lord of the Rings: a city on a hill in the middle of a plain ringed by mountains, and a horse on the banner behind the Jarl's throne, like Rohan's (from the video, unverified).

items.title: "I Saw a Dragon!"
items.location: Riverwood, Hilde (on your first visit to the village)
items.description: Old Hilde shouts "A dragon! I saw a dragon!", echoing a song line from the musical Pete's Dragon (1977).

items.title: Heljarchen Hall and TES: Arena
items.location: Heljarchen Hall, the Pale (the plot is sold at the White Hall in Dawnstar, Hearthfire)
items.description: The estate is most likely named after Helarchen Creek, a settlement roughly in this area in the first game of the series, The Elder Scrolls: Arena.

items.title: Rats in the Cellar
items.location: Any Hearthfire home where adopted children live
items.description: Some time after you move in, the children may complain about noises in the basement, and skeevers show up there. The video's author thinks it's a nod to the rat jobs of the Fighters Guild in Morrowind (Balmora) and Oblivion. Skeever attacks on the house are confirmed; the link to earlier games is the author's theory.

items.title: Order of the Black Worm Ritual
items.location: Hob's Fall Cave, Winterhold Hold (where Pantea's Flute is)
items.description: In the cave you hear the screams of Larina, the bard who stole Pantea's Flute. You can't save her: the necromancers sacrifice her. Sneak up to the altar and you can hear them pray to the God of Worms to blacken a soul gem and revive the Order of the Black Worm. The order was destroyed at the end of the Mages Guild questline in Oblivion.
tips: You need good Sneak to reach the altar unseen and hear the whole ritual

items.title: Dervenin of Mania
items.location: Solitude, the streets near the Blue Palace
items.description: Dervenin, the beggar who starts "The Mind of Madness", appeared before in Shivering Isles for Oblivion, where he was the High Priest of Mania. The video's author notes that he wears a beard, even though Sheogorath banned beards in the Shivering Isles.

items.title: The Reaper: the Soul Cairn's Secret Boss
items.location: Soul Cairn (Dawnguard): three Reaper Gem Fragments lie in chests across the Cairn; the pedestal is in the Reaper's Lair
items.description: Collect the three Reaper Gem Fragments and place them on the pedestal in the Reaper's Lair, and the Reaper appears with three bonemen. He's a hooded ghostly executioner with red eyes and an iron battleaxe who spits green slime. The reward is modest: three black soul gems and a daedra heart. The video's author sees a nod to the Lich boss from Gauntlet: Dark Legacy.
tips: The Reaper is fairly weak, so don't waste your best potions on him

items.title: Bright Bird in Riverwood
items.location: Riverwood, the tree by the bridge
items.description: A bright, parrot-like bird is stuck in the crown of the tree by the bridge. The author thinks it's left over from wildlife cut from the game. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Arrow-Eating Shrines
items.location: Solitude, Temple of the Divines
items.description: Arrows shot at the shrines of the Nine in the temple vanish without a trace, while those hitting next to them stick as usual. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Giant Namira's Rot
items.location: Blackreach: go down the stairs from the Alftand entrance, then southwest, under the porch of a Dwemer building with Falmer
items.description: The only place in the game where Namira's Rot mushrooms are almost ten times larger than usual.

items.title: Sabjorn's Hidden Black-Briar Mead
items.location: Honningbrew Meadery near Whiterun, Sabjorn's bedroom upstairs
items.description: Sabjorn trashes his rivals' Black-Briar mead, yet under his bed sits a bottle of Black-Briar mead in a bowl.

items.title: The Word on Storn's Chest
items.location: Skaal Village, Solstheim (the quest "The Fate of the Skaal")
items.description: When Storn Crag-Strider reads the Black Book, dragon runes appear on his chest: it's the unique, unobtainable armor Word Chest. The rune reads "Dov" (dragon), the third word of the Bend Will shout, which you learn right then.

items.title: The White-Eyed Sarethi Sisters
items.location: Sarethi Farm, the Rift (Avrusa and Aduri Sarethi)
items.description: Every Dunmer in Skyrim has red eyes, and Karliah has pale lilac ones. Only the sisters Avrusa and Aduri Sarethi have the third, whitish Dunmer eye color from the character creator. (from the video, unverified)
tips: The sisters' skin color is also unique and not available in the character creator

items.title: Ill Met By Moonlight and Bloodmoon
items.location: Falkreath Jail (Sinding); Bloated Man's Grotto
items.description: Hircine's hunt under a blood-red moon in "Ill Met By Moonlight" nods to Morrowind's Bloodmoon expansion on Solstheim, where the Skaal prophecy of the Bloodmoon is also tied to Hircine's hunt and a choice between werewolves and men.

items.title: The Barrow's Ghost: Wyndelius Gatharian
items.location: Shroud Hearth Barrow, Ivarstead
items.description: The "ghost" scaring Ivarstead is the Dunmer Wyndelius Gatharian, under a Philter of the Phantom. His name echoes the Dunmer Syndelius Gatharian from Oblivion's Shivering Isles expansion.
tips: He's the only source of the Philter of the Phantom
If raised as a dead thrall, he keeps his ghostly look

items.title: Letters of Maven and Christophe
items.location: Riften, Black-Briar Manor (by Maven's bed); Whiterun, The Bannered Mare (on the table in front of Uthgerd)
items.description: Christophe asks Maven's forgiveness and waits for her at The Bannered Mare. Maven's reply lies there too: she promises to send someone for him at night and advises him to pack his things securely, a hint that Maven doesn't forgive.
tips: Read both letters back to back: the second answers the first

items.title: Escape from the Fort Sungard Oubliette
items.location: Fort Sungard, the Reach: the Oubliette tower east of the fort
items.description: The cells are empty; below are a shovel, pickaxes and a pit: the prisoners dug a tunnel but fell into a cave and died. Next to a bandit's body lie the Pickpocket skill book Guide to Better Thieving and the Fort Sungard Jail Key.
tips: The fall is dangerous at low levels
You can also reach the cave from below without clearing the fort

items.title: Khajiit Ears in Anger
items.location: Any Khajiit in combat
items.description: When Khajiit get angry, not just their faces change but also their ears: they flatten back like a real cat's. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Red Eagle's Sword Turns into a Bucket
items.location: Rebel's Cairn, the Reach: the sword in the pedestal at the entrance
items.description: Cast a spell at the sword in the pedestal (Telekinesis, per the video) and it turns into a bucket, like the placeholder items in the Dawnstar museum and at the end of "Forgotten Legend". After you beat the boss, the sword is back and the bucket is gone. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: The Chill: Winterhold's Jail
items.location: An island north of Winterhold
items.description: Winterhold has no jail of its own: convicts are sent to the ice cave called the Chill, guarded by a frost atronach instead of guards. When arresting you, a guard says: "Ha, enjoy the Chill.". Your gear isn't taken, and three more atronachs appear at the exit.
tips: The atronachs reappear every visit and drop frost salts

items.title: Frost and Robert Frost
items.location: Riften, The Bee and Barb: Louis Letrush; the Black-Briar stables
items.description: The quest "Promises to Keep" and the horse Frost reference Robert Frost's poem "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening". Frost's lineage papers list his sire Grane and great-grandsire Sleipnir, horses from Norse myth.
tips: At level 25, Frost has about 560 health and 148 stamina, more than a regular horse

items.title: Burned by the Fireplace
items.location: Volunruud, by the fireplace near the bookcase
items.description: A burnt corpse lies by the fireplace with a scroll of Ice Storm under it: looks like the poor soul tried to fight the fire but ran out of time.

items.title: The Hourglass Maze
items.location: Labyrinthian, Shalidor's Maze
items.description: From above, Shalidor's Maze looks like an hourglass, as described in the book A Minor Maze. It's a nod to the "Riddle of the Hourglass" from the Labyrinthian quest in The Elder Scrolls: Arena.

items.title: A Head with a Coin in Its Mouth
items.location: Labyrinthian: a nook behind shutters
items.description: Behind the shutters is a severed head with a coin in its mouth: a reference to Charon's obol, the fare paid to the ferryman of souls to the land of the dead. (from the video, unverified)

items.title: Herbane's Bestiary and Mzulft
items.location: Mzulft; the book is in Labyrinthian and elsewhere
items.description: Broken Dwarven spiders and spheres lie all over Mzulft and never disappear. In the book Herbane's Bestiary: Automatons, the author describes descending into the darkness of Mzulft and destroying the machines there.

items.title: The Necromancer Amulet in Every Game
items.location: Reward for the quest "Blood on the Ice", Windhelm
items.description: The Necromancer Amulet is Mannimarco's legendary artifact and has appeared in Arena, Daggerfall, Morrowind and Oblivion. Unlike many Daedric artifacts, it's in every game of the series.

items.title: Mercer's Taunts in Irkngthand
items.location: Irkngthand, the quest "Blindsighted"
items.description: Mercer left shadowmarks in Irkngthand: "Guild" ("safe") on a table with three lockpicks before the Grand Cavern, and "Empty" on a chest next to the mirrored message "One Step Ahead". The third mark, "Thieves Cache", is on the pipes at the end of the Slave Pens, with two potions below it.
tips: To reach the "Thieves Cache" mark, climb the pipes along the west wall

items.title: Garmr and CuSith
items.location: Castle Volkihar (Dawnguard)
items.description: The death hounds are named after mythical dogs: Garmr, the four-eyed guardian of Hel's gates in Norse myth, and Cù Sìth, the death-gathering hound of Scottish folklore. Both become followers if you side with the vampires.

items.title: Meaningful Names
items.location: Markarth (Silver-Blood Inn), the path to High Hrothgar, Jorrvaskr
items.description: Hreinn, who's always cleaning up at the inn, has a name meaning "clean" in Icelandic. Klimmek hauls supplies to the Greybeards, and klimmen is Dutch for "to climb". Farkas (Hungarian farkas) and Vilkas (Lithuanian vilkas) both mean "wolf", and Kodlak sounds like the Slavic "vukodlak" (werewolf).

items.title: The Missing Apprentices
items.location: Bodies across Skyrim: Yisra, Ilas-Tei, Borvir and Rundi
items.description: An unfinished College quest: Phinis Gestor was supposed to send you to find his four missing apprentices. The quest isn't in the game, but the apprentices themselves lie dead across Skyrim, each with their belongings.
